when.quote: Before attempting retention, confirm the customer is eligible to close their account. Check these in order:

starts.note: customer: this job starts only when the customer asks to close a credit card. After that, the agent offers each retention option the documents name: another Rho-Bank card, a fee waiver, a downgrade, or the one tier-based retention offer. Any write (a payment, waiver, downgrade, credit or closure) runs only after the customer accepts or authorizes it. If the customer wants to close more than one card, run the whole job once for each card, one card at a time.
starts.quote: Found a better card: Ask what features attracted them. If Rho-Bank offers a card with similar or better benefits, offer to help them apply instead of closing the current account.

tools.not_used: None of the documents this job cites names a tool for the customer to run. The agent unlocks and calls every discoverable tool here itself.
Only the CLI documents name this tool. The closure eligibility checks do not look at payment history.
The closure job never orders a replacement card. A pending replacement only blocks closure; replacing a card is the separate job order_replacement_credit_card.
The closure job only reads dispute status and never files a dispute. Filing is the separate job filing_a_credit_card_transaction_dispute, done only if the customer asks.

steps.do: Compare each business Rho-Bank card's own terms with the features the customer named. Recommend only a card that matches or beats every one of those features, and never one that lacks any of them. Business Platinum Rewards Card: 4.0% on travel, software and media advertising, 1.5% on other purchases, 0% foreign transaction fee, $450.00 standard annual fee, and a first-year promotional fee of 0 for new accounts opened in its promo window (check get_time). Business Gold Rewards Card: 2.5% on operations only, 0% foreign transaction fee, no advertising category. Business Silver Rewards Card: 10.0% on travel and software, 1.5% foreign transaction fee. Business Bronze Rewards Card: flat 1.0%, with a foreign transaction fee. Green Rewards Card: 1.0% foreign transaction fee. Silver Zoom Card: 3.0% on sector-specific spend, 2.5% foreign transaction fee. For travel, advertising and no foreign fee, the match is the Business Platinum Rewards Card. Offer to help the customer apply for it instead of closing. If no card matches, say so and go to retention_offer.

steps.quote: Travel, software, and media advertising purchases earn 4.0%.

steps.do: Compare the terms of every personal Rho-Bank card (see rules) with the features the customer named: reward rate or categories, foreign transaction fee and annual fee. Recommend only a card the customer can apply for that matches or beats them. Never recommend the Diamond Elite Card, which is by invitation only. Recommend the Gold Rewards Card only if the customer has Rho-Bank+. For a high flat rate with no foreign transaction fee: the Platinum Rewards Card earns 10.0% on all eligible purchases, has a 0% foreign transaction fee and a $200.00 annual fee, and gives a $150.00 rebate if $7500.00 is spent in every month of the cardmember year. For travel and software spending: the Silver Rewards Card earns 4.0% on travel and software and 1.0% elsewhere, with a $0.00 annual fee and a 2.75% foreign transaction fee without a premium subscription. Check get_time before mentioning any promotion, and mention it only if its window is open. If no card is similar or better, say so and go to retention_offer. Otherwise, offer to help the customer apply instead of closing.

steps.do: Make ONE retention offer, based on the tier of the card being closed. Entry-tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit. Mid-tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): 2,000 bonus points or a $20 statement credit. Premium and above (Gold, Business Gold, Platinum, Business Platinum, Diamond Elite): 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit. Make the offer only after the concern step for the customer's reason. For found_better_card, a comparable Rho-Bank card must have been presented first (or none matched) and the customer still wants to close. For simplifying_finances or other there is no tailored step, so go straight to this offer.

open_questions: Retention offers allow bonus points, but no document names a tool to post bonus points. If a customer picks points, the agent can only explain and offer the statement credit or a transfer.
'Customer for 2+ years' (annual fee waiver) does not say whether tenure counts from the earliest Rho-Bank account or from the card being closed.
No tailored solution is written for 'simplifying_finances' or 'other'; the workflow goes straight to the tier retention offer.
The dispute-history tool returns disputes by user, not by card; the match to the card relies on card_last4 or transaction, and statuses other than open, under_review and closed are not defined.
The retention protocol orders the checks disputes → replacement → age → balance, while the closure process doc lists balance first; the workflow follows the retention protocol's order.
No document says whether a found_better_card customer who applies for a new Rho-Bank card should also have the old card closed; the workflow keeps it open unless the customer asks again to close it.

The Green Rewards Card's product pages are under business cards, but customers may hold it as a personal card; the tier lists put it in Mid tier either way, and no document says which no-fee downgrade target applies to it.

steps.quote: Unhappy with rewards: Check enrollment in available bonus categories and suggest ways to maximize rewards based on spending patterns.

steps.do: Apologize and gather details. If escalation is warranted, ask the customer whether they want to be transferred, and transfer only if they agree. For a service-related complaint you may offer a modest goodwill credit with apply_statement_credit_8472 (reason 'goodwill_adjustment'), applied only if the customer accepts.
steps.if: closure_reason is negative_experience AND escalation is warranted AND the customer agrees to be transferred
steps.quote: Negative experience: Apologize and gather details. Escalate to a supervisor if warranted. Consider offering a modest goodwill credit for service-related complaints.

steps.do: If the customer still wants to close (including simplifying_finances or other, which have no tailored solution), make one retention offer by card tier. Entry (Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards, Crypto-Cash Back): 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit. Mid (Silver Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom): 2,000 bonus points or a $20 statement credit. Premium and above (Gold, Business Gold, Platinum, Business Platinum, Diamond Elite): 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit. Make only one offer.
steps.if: the customer still wants to close after their concern was addressed
steps.quote: If the customer still wants to close after addressing their concerns, make one retention offer based on their card tier:

steps.do: Unlock apply_statement_credit_8472, then call it with the tier amount. The card stays open and is not closed.

args.amount: tier amount from retention_offer: 5.00 entry, 20.00 mid, 50.00 premium and above

steps.if: the customer accepts the statement-credit retention offer
steps.quote: 'retention_offer': Credit offered to retain a customer

steps.do: If the customer picks the bonus-points option, explain that you cannot find a documented way to post bonus points. Offer the statement credit instead, or a transfer to a human agent if the customer wants one.
steps.if: the customer accepts the bonus-points retention offer
steps.quote: Entry-tier cards: Offer 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit

steps.do: Thank the customer without pressure, then unlock close_credit_card_account_7834 and call it.
steps.if: all four eligibility checks passed AND (there is a closure-reason record within the past year OR the customer declined the retention offer and still wants to close)
steps.quote: If the customer declines the retention offer (or was ineligible due to prior attempts), thank them for being a Rho-Bank customer and proceed with closure. Do not apply pressure.

steps.do: Confirm the closure. Tell the customer a confirmation email and final statement arrive within several business days, that unredeemed rewards can be redeemed for 45 days, and that if an annual fee posted recently, closing within 37 days of it may qualify for a full refund.
steps.if: close_account succeeded
steps.quote: Inform the customer they have 45 days after submitting the closure request to redeem unredeemed rewards; after that, rewards are forfeited.

rules.rule: Check eligibility in this order: pending disputes, pending replacement, account age, outstanding balance. If any check fails, explain what must be resolved and make no retention offer and no closure.
rules.quote: If any requirement is not met, explain what must be resolved and do not proceed with retention offers.

rules.rule: The balance must be $0.00 before closure.
rules.quote: Zero balance required: Your account must have an outstanding balance of $0.00 dollars.

rules.rule: The account must be at least 60 days old.
rules.quote: Minimum account age: Your account must have been open for at least 60 days.

rules.rule: Any replacement order that is not final blocks closure. Proceed only when every order is delivered or cancelled.
rules.quote: If all orders are final (delivered or cancelled), proceed with standard closure checks.

rules.rule: A closure-reason record for this card within the past year means no retention: close directly.
rules.quote: If records exist for this account within that time frame, skip retention offers and proceed directly to processing the closure.

rules.rule: log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 accepts only credit_card_account_id, user_id and closure_reason.
rules.quote: Note: Only these three arguments are accepted. Do not add additional parameters.

rules.rule: Mid-tier retention offer: 2,000 bonus points or a $20 statement credit.
rules.quote: Mid-tier cards: Offer 2,000 bonus points or a $20 statement credit

rules.rule: Premium tier and above retention offer: 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit.
rules.quote: Premium and above: Offer 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit

rules.rule: Entry tier cards: Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card.
rules.quote: Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): Maximum $2500.00

rules.rule: Mid tier cards: Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card.
rules.quote: Mid Tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): Maximum $5000.00

rules.rule: Premium tier cards: Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card. Platinum and Diamond Elite cards rank above premium.
rules.quote: Premium Tier (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card): Maximum $10000.00

rules.rule: A downgrade stays within the same category (personal to personal, business to business).
rules.quote: Customers may only downgrade within the same category (personal to personal, business to business).

rules.rule: Silver Rewards Card earns 4.0% on eligible travel and software purchases.
rules.quote: Pay with your card for eligible travel and software transactions to earn 4.0% back

rules.rule: Silver Rewards Card requires a minimum credit score of 680.
rules.quote: Minimum credit score: $680

rules.rule: Gold Rewards Card earns a flat 2.5% on all purchases.
rules.quote: Cash back on all purchases: 2.5%

rules.rule: Project management and productivity subscriptions count as software/SaaS for the Silver Rewards Card.
rules.quote: Subscription-based productivity suites, collaboration tools, and project management platforms

rules.rule: Do not pressure a customer who declines retention.
rules.quote: If the customer declines the retention offer (or was ineligible due to prior attempts), thank them for being a Rho-Bank customer and proceed with closure. Do not apply pressure.

draft.done_when: For each card the customer asked about, exactly one of these is true and has been told to the customer: (a) a failed eligibility check was explained with what must be resolved; (b) the customer accepted a retention solution or offer (fee waiver, downgrade, new-card application or statement credit) and it was applied, so the card stays open; or (c) close_credit_card_account_7834 succeeded and the post-closure information was given.

when.quote: When a customer needs to pay off their credit card balance using funds from their Rho-Bank checking account, you can process the payment directly.

starts.note: customer: only when the customer asks to pay the balance from their checking account. In a closure, the agent explains that the balance must be paid but does not move money unless the customer authorizes it.
starts.quote: Confirm the payment amount with the customer and obtain authorization to transfer.

info.about: the customer's confirmation of the amount and their authorization to debit checking
info.ask: Shall I pay the outstanding balance on this card from your Rho-Bank checking account?

info.about: which checking account to debit, if the customer has more than one
info.ask: Which checking account would you like to use for this payment?

steps.do: Make sure the customer was verified and logged earlier in this conversation (credit_card_retention_and_account_closure steps lookup_user through log_verification). If not, verify and log now. Do not verify twice.
steps.quote: Verify the customer's identity using standard procedures.

steps.do: Unlock get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847, then call it to get the customer's checking accounts and their balances.
steps.quote: Use get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 to retrieve the bank accounts (checkings, savings) for a customer.

steps.do: Get the credit card's current outstanding balance.
steps.quote: Look up the customer's credit card account to confirm the outstanding balance.

steps.do: Confirm the customer has an open Rho-Bank checking account whose balance covers the payment. The amount must be positive and no more than either the checking balance or the card's outstanding balance. If no checking account exists or funds are short, explain this and do not pay.
steps.quote: Confirm the customer has a Rho-Bank checking account with sufficient funds to cover the payment amount.

steps.do: Tell the customer the amount (the card's outstanding balance) and the checking account to be debited. Get their explicit authorization.
steps.if: check_funds passed
steps.quote: Confirm the payment amount with the customer and obtain authorization to transfer.

steps.do: Unlock pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 with unlock_discoverable_agent_tool, then call it with call_discoverable_agent_tool. Report the new balances from the confirmation, then return to the closure job's check_balance.

args.checking_account_id: get_bank_accounts result (the checking account the customer chose)
args.amount: the card's outstanding balance from get_card_balance

steps.if: check_funds passed AND the customer authorized the payment
steps.quote: Unlock the pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 tool using unlock_discoverable_agent_tool.

rules.rule: The payment amount must be positive and must not exceed the checking balance or the card's outstanding balance.
rules.quote: amount (float, required): The payment amount in dollars. Must be positive and cannot exceed the checking account balance or the credit card outstanding balance.

rules.rule: Confirm sufficient checking funds before paying.
rules.quote: Look up the customer's checking account to confirm sufficient funds.

draft.done_when: Either pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 succeeded and the customer was told the new balances (and, in a closure, the card balance is confirmed $0.00), or the customer was told why the payment could not be made.
